clue.text: It's of little help to a European trying to make his mark

definitions.text: It's of little help to a European trying to make his mark

blocks.clueFragment: of little help to a European trying to make his mark
blocks.note: surface reading: something barely useful to a European striving to make an impression
setter's reading: a German assembling enough small coins to make up one Deutschmark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is not a mark of distinction but the old German currency; the answer was its hundredth part, so one coin did little towards a whole mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The pfennig was a tiny coin, a hundredth of a Deutschmark, so a single one contributed almost nothing towards making a full mark.

clue.text: Saw lions disappear at the end of every summer?

definitions.text: lions disappear at the end of every summer?

blocks.note: first meaning: a saw is an old proverb

blocks.clueFragment: lions disappear at the end of every summer?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a group of lions departs ahead of autumn, which Americans call the fall

explanation.surface: A naturalist noticed the lions vanishing every year as summer ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is a noun meaning a proverb. A group of lions is a pride, and the season after summer is the fall in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, and this one warns that arrogance comes before ruin.

clue.text: I get weary, me - it's another way for those who've retired!

indicators.note: going another way means the words before are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
to tire is to grow weary
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tired of their job claims retirement is simply another route through life.
explanation.walkthrough: I + TIRE + ME, read backwards, gives EMERITI.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are professors and other office holders who have retired but keep their title honorifically.

clue.text: Some drug sounds like grass

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to say the drug word aloud and spell another word that matches it

blocks.note: narc is a clipped form of narcotic, so only part of the drug word

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain drug smells or seems like cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like cannabis to go with the drug, but it is the British slang verb or noun for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass and a nark are both police informers who tell tales on criminals.

clue.text: See 1
Commander's commander in sort of novel that could go either way?

indicators.note: something that could go either way reads identically from the front or from the back

blocks.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander, here in the possessive
the same Ottoman title again

explanation.surface: A senior officer's own superior features in a novel whose plot is evenly balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is also a cast-iron range cooker, a symbol of the comfortable English country kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga saga is a genre of popular fiction about middle-class family life in the English countryside.

clue.text: Legal officer presenting a longer entreaty when in difficulties

indicators.note: letters in difficulties are in trouble and thrown out of their proper order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer in trouble makes an ever more drawn-out plea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Attorney-General is the chief law officer advising the government, so plainly a legal officer.

clue.text: Language in a slogan that's silly - Number 10's spinning

indicators.note: a silly arrangement is a foolish one, so these letters are jumbled
spinning turns something round, so the number words are read backwards

blocks.note: letters to be jumbled
No. is the standard abbreviation for number
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Spin doctors at 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence, produce a daft slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Saxon is the name for Old English, the tongue spoken in England before the Norman Conquest; it also means blunt, earthy speech.

clue.text: A follower of Aquinas - not hard sort of philosopher?

indicators.note: not hard says the abbreviation for hard must be dropped from what precedes

blocks.note: taken as written
a Thomist follows the teaching of Thomas Aquinas
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A disciple of Aquinas who isn't rigorous might be some kind of philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: A THOMIST without its H gives ATOMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomist holds that all matter consists of indivisible particles, a school going back to Democritus.

clue.text: Around time of austerity, pay perversely is more than enough

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the period of austerity
done perversely means done in a contrary, wrong-headed way, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: letters to be jumbled
Lent is the season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Paying out lavishly during a lean period seems excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplenty is a postpositive adjective meaning in abundance, so there is more than enough.

clue.text: Serious-minded one keeping fledglings within view?

blocks.note: a parent bird keeps its fledglings inside its nest

explanation.surface: A conscientious parent bird keeps watch over its fledglings.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no sound signal beyond 'view?': the question mark asks you to take the phrase as a pun, since in a non-rhotic British accent the answer is said just like 'in a nest'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in earnest is to be sincere and serious rather than joking.

clue.text: After good quarrel, left with snarl

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a row is a noisy argument
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: After a proper argument, someone walks away growling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the letters for good first, with the quarrel following.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl and a snarl are both low, angry throaty noises, from dogs or bad-tempered people.

clue.text: Change when season comes around

indicators.note: coming around means turning about, so the season word is read backwards

blocks.note: tide is an old word for a season, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Things alter as the seasons turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to alter or revise it, so the verb is a synonym of change.

clue.text: What's tossed by Scot heading off with two men - one his compatriot

indicators.note: with its heading off, the tossed object loses its first letter

blocks.note: the caber is the tree trunk thrown in Highland games
Don is a man's name
Ian is another man's name, a Scottish one

explanation.surface: A Scottish caber tosser sets off with two companions, one of them a fellow Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: (C)ABER + DON + IAN. 'Two men' supplies two names in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdonian comes from Aberdeen in Scotland, so is a fellow countryman of the caber-tossing Scot.

clue.text: Dogged girl being devious?

indicators.note: being devious means taking a crooked, indirect course, so the letters stray from their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A determined young woman with a scheming streak.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer too: a persistent woman deviously chasing a rich partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold-digger is a woman who pursues wealthy men for their money, persistently and with calculation.

clue.text: Warning - superior gent has very little money

indicators.note: the gent has something inside him, so his letters hold the small sum

blocks.note: a toff is an upper-class, well-dressed man
1p, one penny, written with a figure one that looks like I

explanation.surface: A posh man is short of cash, which serves as a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-penny coin is written 1p, and the figure 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a discreet piece of advance information, often alerting someone to danger.

clue.text: Sign of something wrong with performance? See about that, just!

indicators.note: the See goes about, or around, the sign and the performance

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see
a cross marks an error
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A critic spots a flaw in a show and tells you to look into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as an exclamation, 'exactly!' and 'just!' both mean precisely so, agreeing completely.

clue.text: One who fights partner no end, love being deficient

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the partner word is removed
being deficient means falling short, so the love word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a mate is a partner
to adore is to love

explanation.surface: Someone constantly bickering with their spouse, lacking affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is not O here but the verb ADORE, cut short like MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, so one who fights in the ring.

clue.text: Army officer about to take over a holiday island

blocks.note: a major is an army rank
c. for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military man is poised to seize a resort island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'take over' means sit on top of: the abbreviation for about goes above the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest Balearic island, a hugely popular Mediterranean holiday destination.

clue.text: Medal for bravery that is associated with the ultimate in sacrifices first given to soldiers

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written; 'first given' puts it at the front
MM is the Military Medal
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gallantry medal honouring the supreme sacrifice is awarded to troops.
explanation.walkthrough: TO goes first, then MM + IE + S. Tommies is the old nickname for British private soldiers, from Tommy Atkins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, has long been the nickname for an ordinary British soldier.

clue.text: Go through childhood with small gang of people around

indicators.note: the gang goes around the abbreviation, holding it inside

blocks.note: a group is a small band of people
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Passing through one's early years with a little band of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow up is to mature from a child into an adult, passing through childhood.

clue.text: Suffer in submission to divine power endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the divine word is cut away

blocks.note: under someone is subject to them
a god is a divine power

explanation.surface: Someone endures suffering in perpetual obedience to a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo an ordeal is to experience or endure it, much as one suffers it.

clue.text: One maniac on the loose in the early part of year must be brought to book

indicators.note: something on the loose runs free, so the letters scatter out of order
in places the scrambled letters inside the early part of the year

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
letters to be jumbled
Jan is short for January

explanation.surface: A lunatic escaping in January must be caught and punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' sounds like facing justice, but the book is the definition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is Daphne du Maurier's 1936 novel set on Bodmin Moor, so it is a book.

clue.text: A mostly gloomy time in the Jewish calendar

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the gloomy word, so its tail goes

blocks.note: taken as written
dark is gloomy

explanation.surface: A rather sombre period in the Jewish year.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is the twelfth month of the Jewish religious year, falling around February and March.

clue.text: Gas gets central heating device functioning

blocks.note: rad is a short, informal word for a radiator
on means working

explanation.surface: The boiler fires up and the radiator starts working.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, element 86.

clue.text: Difficult problem when word of denial is heard

indicators.note: is heard means the denial word counts by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: not is the word that denies, and the K of the spelling is silent

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arises when someone hears the word 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty or tangled matter is a hard problem, as in untying the knot of a dilemma.

clue.text: Deploring bankruptcy, getting $1,000

blocks.note: financial ruin is bankruptcy
a grand is a thousand dollars, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: Lamenting going bust after receiving a thousand dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing something is regretting or lamenting it, so the participle matches deploring.

clue.text: Numbers recorded this mysteriously flowering plant

blocks.note: first meaning: in the Book of Numbers a priest's staff miraculously blossoms and bears almonds
second meaning: a common name for mullein, a tall yellow-flowered wild plant

explanation.surface: Statistics were logged on a plant that bloomed inexplicably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' is the fourth book of the Bible, where the staff of Moses' brother sprouts overnight; the same name is given to mullein and goldenrod.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a common name for great mullein, a tall yellow-flowered wild plant, named after the biblical staff.

clue.text: Like stars around Uruguay not seen in our hemisphere

indicators.note: the star word goes around the country's abbreviation, holding it inside

blocks.note: astral means relating to stars
U is the international vehicle code for Uruguay

explanation.surface: Stars visible from South America cannot be seen from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter writes from the northern hemisphere, so southern things are those not seen there.
explanation.definitionFit: Austral means southern, describing places and stars of the southern hemisphere, invisible from northern latitudes.

clue.text: Anticlimax coming back to earth?

blocks.note: first meaning: a disappointing outcome after high hopes
second meaning, read literally: lowered to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal second sense: something lowered back down to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-down is a disappointment that deflates expectations, and taken literally means being lowered down again.
